paragraphs: Recognizing an image or video can require connecting information from distant locations or moments. Convolutional networks commonly acquire this broader view by becoming deeper, which the paper identifies as inefficient. The proposed double attention block gives later convolutional layers access to information gathered across the entire input space.

The block works in two stages. First, second-order attention pooling collects global features into a compact set. A second attention operation then selects and distributes relevant features to individual locations. This separates collecting useful information from deciding where it should be used. The component can be inserted into existing networks, making the approach an architectural addition rather than requiring a completely new recognition system.

Experiments cover both image and action recognition. On ImageNet-1k, ResNet-50 with these blocks outperformed ResNet-152 while using over 40% fewer parameters and fewer floating-point operations. The authors also report state-of-the-art results on Kinetics and UCF-101 with substantially higher efficiency than recent work. These results support the value of explicitly sharing global features for the evaluated recognition tasks.
neurips-2018-a-2-nets-double-attention-n.tldr: Double attention gathers global image or video features and redistributes them locally, improving recognition while reducing computation in the reported experiments.

paragraphs: Learning a policy becomes harder when other agents influence outcomes and some information remains hidden. This paper examines policy gradient and actor-critic methods in that setting. These approaches adjust a parameterized decision rule to improve a score based on discounted rewards, but their behavior also depends on how interacting agents learn.

The authors connect several candidate policy updates to regret minimization and established multiagent learning techniques. These connections yield previously unknown convergence guarantees for one-shot and tabular cases. The distinction matters: the theoretical results concern those settings, while the paper also explores function approximation in more complex sequential games.

The experimental application is model-free learning in zero-sum games with imperfect information, using benchmark Poker domains. The authors evaluate play against fixed opponents and learning through self-play. They report empirical convergence toward approximate Nash equilibria at rates similar to or better than a baseline model-free algorithm for zero-sum games. This was achieved without domain-specific reductions of the state space, supporting the practical relevance of the proposed updates beyond the simpler theoretical cases.
neurips-2018-actor-critic-policy-optimiz.tldr: The paper connects actor-critic policy updates to regret minimization, establishing guarantees in simpler settings and demonstrating approximate equilibrium learning in Poker.

paragraphs: When many generative adversarial network algorithms report strong results, it can be difficult to tell whether their differences reflect better methods or better experimental circumstances. This paper addresses that comparison problem through a large empirical study of leading GAN models and the measures used to evaluate them.

The central finding is that most tested models can achieve similar scores when given enough hyperparameter tuning and random restarts. This suggests that some apparent progress may come from spending more computation on finding successful configurations. It does not establish that all GAN algorithms are equivalent; it shows why tuning effort matters when interpreting the evaluated results.

The authors also introduce datasets on which precision and recall can be computed, addressing some limitations of existing evaluation measures. Across their study, they find no evidence that a tested algorithm consistently outperforms the non-saturating GAN. Together, these findings motivate more systematic evaluation: a compelling comparison needs to account for how models are tuned and what the chosen measures actually reveal.
neurips-2018-are-gans-created-equal-a-la.tldr: A large GAN comparison finds that tuning and restarts often close performance gaps, motivating more systematic evaluation of algorithmic progress.

paragraphs: Learning a new task from only a few examples leaves considerable uncertainty about which model best explains the observations. This paper develops Bayesian model-agnostic meta-learning to represent that uncertainty during rapid adaptation. Its aim is to learn how to infer a distribution over plausible models from a small task dataset.

The method combines gradient-based meta-learning with nonparametric variational inference in a probabilistic framework. During adaptation, it can represent uncertainty more complex than a simple Gaussian approximation. During the meta-update, a separate Bayesian mechanism is designed to prevent overfitting at the level where information is shared across tasks. The approach therefore addresses both uncertainty within a new task and overfitting across the training tasks.

The method retains gradient-based learning and applies to several kinds of problems, including reinforcement learning. Experiments examine sinusoidal regression, image classification, active learning, and reinforcement learning, with results supporting its accuracy and robustness. The contribution is a way to combine fast task adaptation with richer uncertainty modeling across these different learning settings.
neurips-2018-bayesian-model-agnostic-met.tldr: Bayesian model-agnostic meta-learning combines fast gradient-based adaptation with richer uncertainty inference and a Bayesian mechanism against meta-level overfitting.

paragraphs: Connectionist Temporal Classification, or CTC, trains models to map one sequence to another using dynamic programming. It has been useful for tasks such as recognizing speech and text in images. The paper focuses on a weakness of this objective: its predicted distributions can become sharply concentrated and overconfident, which the authors identify as a symptom of overfitting.

The proposed remedy adds regularization based on maximum conditional entropy. This discourages overly concentrated distributions and encourages the model to explore alternatives during learning. A second contribution uses entropy to prune feasible CTC paths, removing alignments judged unreasonable. These two changes address different parts of the problem: confidence in the learned distribution and the collection of possible sequence alignments.

Experiments on scene text recognition show consistent improvements over the CTC baseline without changing the training settings. The findings support the usefulness of adjusting the learning objective and alignment handling within an existing sequence-learning framework. The stated experimental evidence concerns scene text recognition, even though CTC itself is used in other sequence tasks.
neurips-2018-connectionist-temporal-clas.tldr: Entropy regularization and entropy-based alignment pruning improve CTC scene text recognition in the reported experiments.

paragraphs: Learning a directed acyclic graph means identifying directed relationships while ensuring that no path loops back to its starting point. Searching over possible graphs is difficult because the number of candidates grows superexponentially with the number of nodes. Traditional approaches use local heuristics to keep the search within the set of graphs without cycles.

This paper replaces that discrete search formulation with continuous optimization over real-valued matrices. Its central contribution is a characterization of acyclicity that is both smooth and exact. Smoothness allows numerical optimization methods to work with the condition, while exactness means the condition captures the absence of cycles rather than merely approximating it.

The resulting problem can be handled efficiently by standard numerical algorithms, simplifying implementation. The authors report that their method outperforms existing approaches without requiring graph restrictions such as bounded treewidth or a bound on incoming edges. The broader significance is that a difficult structural requirement can be expressed in a form compatible with continuous optimization, opening a different route to learning graph structure.
neurips-2018-dags-with-no-tears-continuo.tldr: An exact, smooth characterization of acyclicity turns directed graph structure learning into continuous optimization over matrices.

paragraphs: Hierarchical reinforcement learning divides decision-making between higher-level and lower-level controllers. It promises to handle complex behavior, but many methods require substantial task-specific design and fresh interactions for training. This paper develops an approach intended to reduce both burdens, making hierarchical learning more practical for problems such as robotic control.

Higher-level controllers automatically learn and propose goals that supervise lower-level controllers. Both levels train from off-policy experience, allowing previously collected interactions to be reused. Reuse creates a particular difficulty: as the lower-level controller changes, a higher-level action can produce different behavior. The authors introduce an off-policy correction to address this changing relationship between levels.

Experiments show simulated robots learning complex behaviors, including pushing objects and using them to reach target locations. These behaviors were learned from a few million samples, described as equivalent to a few days of real-time interaction. The method substantially outperformed several prior hierarchical approaches in the reported comparisons. The findings support combining automatically learned goals with corrected experience reuse to reduce the interactions needed for hierarchical learning.
neurips-2018-data-efficient-hierarchical.tldr: Automatically learned goals and an off-policy correction let hierarchical controllers reuse experience and learn complex simulated robot behaviors more efficiently.

paragraphs: Sometimes the important question is how a causal system changes between two conditions. Learning a complete graph for each condition can be an unnecessarily large intermediate task, especially when both graphs are dense. This paper directly estimates their differences, motivated in part by changes in gene regulatory networks.

The setting assumes independent, identically distributed samples from each of two causal directed acyclic graph models that share a topological order. The algorithm first tests whether regression coefficients remain invariant across the datasets to identify the connections in the difference graph without directions. It then tests invariance of regression residual variances to orient some of those connections.

The authors provide a provably consistent method for estimating differences directly, avoiding separate reconstruction of the two full graphs. The shared ordering is part of the stated problem, and the orientation step identifies directions for some edges rather than promising a fully directed answer. Simulations and applications to ovarian cancer gene expression and T-cell activation demonstrate the method's properties and its use in studying changing biological relationships.
neurips-2018-direct-estimation-of-differ.tldr: For two causal DAGs sharing a topological order, invariance tests estimate graph differences directly and orient some changed connections.

paragraphs: A network can leave observable traces even when its connections are hidden. Information spreading or infections moving between nodes produce sequences of arrival times that contain clues about the underlying structure. This paper asks how those traces can support a generative model of a network that changes over time.

The proposed framework uses cascade infection times and a mixture of coupled hierarchical Dirichlet processes to construct a nonparametric dynamic network model. It infers evolving community structure while producing an explicit predictive distribution over network edges. The goal goes beyond identifying connections that visibly carried a particular cascade: the model also assigns predictions to edges absent from observed transmissions and edges that may appear later.

Experiments on synthetic and real-world networks support the effectiveness of the approach. Its main contribution is to turn indirect observations of spreading processes into a probabilistic account of changing network structure. Expressing the output as a predictive distribution retains the distinction between observed cascade events and inferred or future connections, whose existence is being predicted.
neurips-2018-dynamic-network-model-from-.tldr: A probabilistic model uses cascade infection times to infer evolving communities and predict hidden or future network edges.

paragraphs: An inter-atomic potential energy surface describes how a system's energy depends on its atomic configuration. Modeling this relationship is central to molecular modeling in materials science, chemistry, and computational biology. This paper introduces Deep Potential–Smooth Edition, or DeepPot-SE, an end-to-end learned model intended to represent these energy surfaces efficiently.

The architecture builds several physical and computational properties into the model. It preserves the system's natural symmetries and is extensive, so its energy representation respects the size dependence of the system. It is also continuously differentiable, providing smoothly varying derivatives. Its computational cost scales linearly with system size, addressing the need to represent larger collections of atoms efficiently.

The authors report accuracy comparable to ab initio quantum mechanics models for a wide variety of systems. Their demonstrations include both finite and extended systems, spanning organic molecules, metals, semiconductors, and insulators. The contribution combines these reported representational capabilities with structural properties guaranteed by construction. That combination matters because matching energy values and respecting the physical organization of an energy model are complementary requirements.
neurips-2018-end-to-end-symmetry-preserv.tldr: DeepPot-SE models atomic energies with reported quantum-mechanical accuracy while preserving physical symmetries, smoothness, extensivity, and linear scaling.

paragraphs: Word embeddings represent words as points in a space where similar meanings are expected to be close together. The authors find that embeddings learned in several tasks also separate words according to how frequently they occur. A rare word can therefore sit far from a common word with a similar meaning, weakening the usefulness of the representation.

FRAGE addresses this frequency bias with adversarial training that blurs the boundary between embeddings of common and rare words. The purpose is to reduce the separation associated with frequency, which the paper identifies as particularly harmful for rare words. The approach targets a basic representation used inside many language models, so the same issue can affect several downstream tasks.

The study evaluates the method on ten datasets across word similarity, language modeling, machine translation, and text classification. It reports higher performance than the baselines in all four tasks. These results support reducing frequency-related structure in embeddings as a useful intervention across the evaluated applications, rather than treating frequency separation as harmless organization of the representation space.
neurips-2018-frage-frequency-agnostic-wo.tldr: FRAGE uses adversarial training to reduce frequency-based separation in word embeddings and improves results across four evaluated language tasks.

paragraphs: Translation requires preserving meaning across different linguistic forms. This paper introduces Generative Neural Machine Translation, a latent-variable architecture designed to model the semantics shared by source and target sentences. It extends an encoder-decoder model with a hidden representation encouraged to capture sentence meaning independently of the language used.

That representation gives the model a way to account for shared meaning within its translation architecture. On ordinary translation tasks, the authors report competitive BLEU scores. When words are missing from the source sentence, they report superior performance. The latter finding supports the usefulness of the proposed semantic representation when the input provides incomplete information.

The framework is also extended to multilingual translation and semi-supervised learning without adding parameters. With limited paired training data, the authors report a substantial reduction in overfitting. They also find it effective for translating between language pairs absent from training. Together, these findings suggest that modeling a shared latent representation can help the evaluated system use limited, incomplete, or differently paired language evidence.
neurips-2018-generative-neural-machine-t.tldr: A language-agnostic latent representation supports competitive translation, improved handling of missing source words, and learning with limited or unseen language pairings.

paragraphs: Artificial neurons typically combine weighted inputs linearly before further processing. Biological dendrites can behave differently: nearby synaptic inputs can influence one another, creating local nonlinear interactions. This paper takes that observation as inspiration for dendritic neural networks, or DENNs, which explicitly model such local nonlinearities.

The proposed structure aims to increase what a network can represent while retaining efficient inference. Its additional expressive power comes from interactions within the input-processing structure of a neuron. In supervised learning experiments, the authors observe increased fitting power, supporting the claim that these localized nonlinearities can represent relationships that regular neural networks capture less effectively.

The paper also investigates whether the locality of those interactions helps performance on unseen data. Across 121 classification tasks from the UCI repository, DENNs outrank the naive deep network architectures used in the comparison. This provides empirical support for improved generalization in those tests. The contribution thus links a biologically motivated architectural change to both greater fitting capacity and reported improvements in classification performance.
neurips-2018-improved-expressivity-throu.tldr: Dendritic neural networks add localized nonlinear input interactions, increasing fitting power and improving generalization in the reported classification comparisons.

paragraphs: A prediction system may need to pay a cost to obtain each additional feature at test time. Active feature acquisition asks which information to collect and when enough has been gathered to make a prediction. This paper learns those decisions together with the classifier, aiming to balance predictive performance against acquisition cost.

A reinforcement learning agent chooses between collecting another feature and stopping to predict. The classifier is trained jointly with that agent. To represent the information already acquired, the authors introduce a feature-level set encoding that is unchanged by the order in which features were collected. This handles subsets of varying sizes and substantially reduces the agent's search space.

Evaluation uses a purpose-designed synthetic dataset and several medical datasets. The authors report acquisition sequences for diagnosis that agree meaningfully with human knowledge, alongside better prediction performance and lower acquisition cost than all evaluated baselines. The results support treating information collection and prediction as a coupled learning problem, with the set representation helping organize decisions over incomplete feature collections.
neurips-2018-joint-active-feature-acquis.tldr: Jointly learning a classifier and feature-acquisition agent improves the reported balance between prediction quality and information-gathering cost.

paragraphs: Batch Normalization relies on statistics estimated from a mini-batch to normalize a network's internal representations. With very small batches, those estimates can become unreliable. This is especially relevant when memory-intensive tasks such as detection, segmentation, or video processing constrain how many examples can be processed together.

Kalman Normalization treats the network's layers as a connected system. When estimating statistics for one layer, it considers the distributions of preceding layers, drawing on the principle of Kalman filtering. This gives normalization access to information across layers instead of estimating each layer's statistics in isolation. The approach can also extend existing normalization variants, including Group Normalization.

For ResNet50 on ImageNet with batch size four, the abstract reports 3.4% lower error than Batch Normalization. It also reports an advantage at typical batch sizes, where other evaluated Batch Normalization variants degraded. Results on COCO 2017 further show that the method can outperform Batch Normalization and its variants in detection and segmentation. These findings support cross-layer estimation as a practical response to unreliable small-batch statistics.
neurips-2018-kalman-normalization-normal.tldr: Kalman Normalization uses information from preceding layers to estimate normalization statistics, improving reported results especially with small batches.

paragraphs: Determinantal point processes are probabilistic models for selecting sets of items. In their symmetric form, they describe repulsive behavior, making them useful when a selected set should be diverse. This paper studies a new class called signed DPPs, which relax symmetry and allow attractive behavior as well.

Allowing attraction expands the kinds of relationships the model can describe: some items may tend to occur together. The authors lay a foundation for learning these models through the method of moments, connecting statistical information about selected sets to a matrix reconstruction problem. The relevant matrices satisfy a specific condition: each off-diagonal entry equals either its transposed counterpart or its negative.

The central technical result is a polynomial-time solution to the principal minor assignment problem for that matrix class. This supplies a computational ingredient for the proposed learning route. The contribution is therefore both representational and algorithmic: it introduces DPPs with a broader range of interactions and establishes a tractable reconstruction result under the stated matrix restriction.
neurips-2018-learning-signed-determinant.tldr: Signed DPPs allow attractive item relationships, with a polynomial-time matrix reconstruction result providing a foundation for moment-based learning.

paragraphs: A model can fit its training examples perfectly and still perform well on new data, even when training labels contain substantial noise. This challenges the idea that interpolation necessarily indicates harmful overfitting. The paper develops theory for specific local prediction rules to help explain how exact fitting can coexist with good generalization.

The analysis covers geometric simplicial interpolation and nearest-neighbor methods with singular weights. For these schemes, the authors prove consistency or near-consistency in classification and regression. These results concern how prediction risk behaves as more data become available. They establish that fitting the observations exactly need not prevent the analyzed procedures from approaching good population-level performance.

Under some standard statistical assumptions, the nearest-neighbor schemes also achieve optimal rates. The scope of those guarantees is the particular schemes and assumptions studied, rather than every interpolating model. The paper additionally suggests an explanation for adversarial examples and discusses connections to kernel methods and random forests. Those connections position the local analysis as a step toward understanding a broader empirical phenomenon.
neurips-2018-overfitting-or-perfect-fitt.tldr: Theory for local interpolating predictors shows that exact training fit can coexist with consistency and, under stated assumptions, optimal statistical rates.

paragraphs: Semantic correspondence means matching locations across images that depict similar kinds of content. Dense correspondence requires making those matches throughout the images. This paper introduces recurrent transformer networks that solve the problem by repeatedly estimating how one image should be spatially transformed to align with the other.

Each estimated transformation is used to produce aligned convolutional activations, the internal visual features used by the network. The process then repeats, refining both the spatial transformation and the feature representations. The authors show that directly estimating the relationship between an image pair can achieve greater accuracy than independently normalizing each image with spatial transformer networks.

The paper also presents a classification-based loss for weakly supervised training. This supplies a way to train the correspondence model within the proposed iterative framework. The resulting networks achieve reported state-of-the-art performance on several semantic correspondence benchmarks. The central idea is that alignment and representation refinement can help one another across successive steps, improving the final matches between semantically similar images.
neurips-2018-recurrent-transformer-netwo.tldr: Recurrent transformer networks iteratively refine pairwise image transformations and aligned features to improve dense semantic correspondence.

paragraphs: Remembering information over time does not by itself establish that a network can reason about relationships within that information. This paper investigates that distinction in memory-based neural networks. The authors first find that standard memory architectures can struggle on tasks requiring an understanding of how entities connect to one another.

They introduce a Relational Memory Core, or RMC, to improve those capabilities. The module uses multi-head dot product attention so that memories can interact. Its purpose is to make relationships among remembered information available to the recurrent computation, addressing a weakness that simply retaining information for longer would not necessarily resolve.

The evaluation spans reinforcement learning, program evaluation, and language modeling. The authors report large gains in BoxWorld and Mini PacMan, as well as improvements in program evaluation and language modeling. They also report state-of-the-art results on WikiText-103, Project Gutenberg, and GigaWord. These findings support explicitly enabling interactions among memories in the tested sequential tasks, where useful decisions can depend on relationships across stored information.
neurips-2018-relational-recurrent-neural.tldr: A Relational Memory Core lets stored memories interact through attention, improving results across reasoning, reinforcement learning, and language modeling tasks.

paragraphs: Large matrices can be compressed by selecting informative columns. This paper develops a deterministic selection method based on ridge leverage scores, which balance low-rank approximation with regularization. The resulting sketch contains actual columns of the original matrix, aiding interpretation, while deterministic selection produces repeatable results without sampling failure probability.

The authors prove approximation guarantees for column subset selection and preservation of projection costs, both with a factor of one plus epsilon. They also provide an additive-multiplicative spectral bound. Under the additional assumption that ridge leverage scores decay according to a power law, the deterministic method is provably as accurate as randomized algorithms. That comparison explicitly depends on the stated decay assumption.

The paper then applies the sketch to ridge regression. Ordinary ridge regularization often leaves many small but nonzero coefficients. Using the selected columns and a particular regularization parameter instead forces coefficients to zero while retaining a provable one-plus-epsilon statistical risk bound. This makes the approach an interesting alternative to elastic net regularization, combining column selection with controlled prediction risk.
neurips-2018-ridge-regression-and-provab.tldr: Deterministic ridge leverage score sampling yields interpretable matrix sketches with approximation guarantees and supports sparse ridge regression with bounded statistical risk.

paragraphs: Learning from long sequences requires connecting current outcomes to events far in the past. Back-propagation through time sends training information backward through every intervening computational step, which can become prohibitively expensive. This paper explores whether associations between current states and remembered past states can provide shorter routes for assigning credit.

The proposed algorithm learns an attention mechanism that connects the current state to relevant earlier states. It then back-propagates through only a few of these temporal skip connections. The motivating analogy is being reminded of a past memory: an association can link distant moments without replaying every state between them. The paper studies this principle computationally rather than establishing it as a biological mechanism.

On tasks with particularly long dependencies, the method matches or outperforms regular and truncated back-propagation through time. It also transfers to longer sequences substantially better than LSTMs trained with back-propagation through time or full self-attention. These results support sparse learned connections as useful paths for credit assignment in the evaluated long-sequence settings.
neurips-2018-sparse-attentive-backtracki.tldr: Sparse Attentive Backtracking routes training credit through learned links to past states, improving long-dependency learning and transfer in reported experiments.

paragraphs: Randomized coordinate descent tackles high-dimensional optimization by choosing coordinate directions for its updates. This paper proposes accelerating it by expanding the collection of directions available for sampling. Alongside the original coordinates, the method can select a few spectral or conjugate directions that provide additional ways to move through the optimization space.

The analysis shows that adding more of these directions improves the convergence rate. The resulting progression connects the linear rate of randomized coordinate descent to a linear rate independent of the condition number. This describes how the rate changes as the direction set is enriched, making the choice of available directions central to the acceleration strategy.

The authors also develop and analyze inexact versions in which the additional directions need only be approximate. This extends the framework beyond requiring exact spectral or conjugate information. Finally, they prove negative results exposing limitations of coordinate descent with importance sampling. Those results motivate changing the set of directions itself as another route to faster optimization.
neurips-2018-stochastic-spectral-and-con.tldr: Adding spectral or conjugate directions to randomized coordinate descent improves its analyzed convergence rate, with extensions allowing approximate directions.

paragraphs: Adversarial examples are maliciously constructed inputs that can undermine a deep learning model's predictions. This paper approaches the problem through detection: it trains the network to make adversarial and normal inputs easier to distinguish, then filters suspicious inputs at test time. The training procedure and detector are designed to work together.

Training minimizes reverse cross-entropy, an alternative to the usual cross-entropy objective. The intended effect is to shape the network's internal representations so that normal and adversarial examples are better separated. At test time, a thresholding rule uses the resulting distinction to filter adversarial inputs. The authors describe the procedure as straightforward to implement with standard algorithms and requiring little additional training cost.

Evaluation covers several attack methods on MNIST and CIFAR-10. The authors report significant improvements in robust prediction across all threat models considered in their adversarial evaluation. This supports the combination of representation-focused training and threshold detection in the tested settings. The reported scope is those evaluations, rather than an unconditional guarantee against every possible adversarial input.
neurips-2018-towards-robust-detection-of.tldr: Reverse cross-entropy training and threshold-based detection improve robust predictions against the attacks evaluated on MNIST and CIFAR-10.

paragraphs: Generating conversational responses requires both variety and coherence. A system that produces little variation can give trivial replies, while poorly controlled variation can produce digressions. This paper introduces the Variational Memory Encoder-Decoder, or VMED, to address that tension by connecting variability in generation to an external memory.

The model uses the external memory as a mixture model. At each time step, each memory read is associated with a mode in a latent mixture distribution. This provides a structured way to represent different possibilities during sequence generation. The design is intended to capture the variability found in conversations while keeping that variability connected to the encoder-decoder's memory mechanism.

The authors compare VMED with other recent approaches on several conversational datasets. They report consistent, significant improvements in both metric-based evaluation and qualitative assessment. These complementary findings support the proposed memory-based treatment of variability in the evaluated dialogue tasks. The contribution is an architectural way to make diverse generation part of the model's evolving latent representation throughout a sequence.
neurips-2018-variational-memory-encoder-.tldr: VMED links external memory reads to a latent mixture distribution, improving conversational generation in reported quantitative and qualitative evaluations.

paragraphs: Strong control performance does not automatically provide a guarantee about a learned policy's behavior. This paper pursues verifiable reinforcement learning by extracting decision tree policies from a trained deep network. Decision trees can represent complex behavior while offering a structure that existing verification techniques can analyze efficiently.

The proposed algorithm, VIPER, combines model compression and imitation learning. It learns a decision tree under guidance from a neural network policy and that policy's Q-function. This addresses the difficulty of training effective tree policies directly. The authors report that VIPER substantially outperforms two baselines, supporting the usefulness of this guided extraction process.

The demonstrations establish different properties in three settings: robustness for a symbolic-state variant of Atari Pong, never losing in a toy Pong-based game, and stability for cart-pole. In every case, the extracted tree matches the original network's performance. These are task-specific verified properties, showing that policy extraction can preserve performance while enabling formal analysis of the resulting controller in the demonstrated environments.
neurips-2018-verifiable-reinforcement-le.tldr: VIPER extracts decision tree policies that match neural policy performance while enabling verified robustness, game outcomes, or stability in three demonstrated settings.
